reason: The hypothesis proposes applying oxide dispersion strengthening (ODS), a known technique from steels (mentioned in P37), to a new class of refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) for combined high-temperature and irradiation conditions. While ODS and RHEA irradiation resistance are individually known, no passage combines them into a single proposal for RHEAs, nor does any passage study ODS-RHEAs. The specific mechanism of oxide particles pinning dislocations and grain boundaries to improve both strength and irradiation stability in RHEAs is a non-trivial synthesis that goes beyond the existing literature.
